name: collapse-down
concept: The element's height collapses toward its top edge, as if a hidden panel folds up beneath it. Use it for closing an expandable row or a details panel.

name: collapse-up
concept: The element's height collapses toward its bottom edge, like a drawer sliding shut from below. Use it for a footer panel or a bottom sheet that tucks away.

name: collapse-vertical-fade
concept: The element shrinks to zero height from its center while it fades out. A softer, symmetric version of a vertical collapse.

name: drawer-close
concept: The element snaps quickly to a small height, then settles flat and fades. It suggests a drawer pushed shut with some momentum.

name: accordion-close
concept: The element's height steps down in even stages before it disappears, like pleats folding flat one after another. Good for accordion panels.

name: squash-flat
concept: The element flattens to almost nothing, bulging slightly wider as it is pressed down, then it fades. Like squashing a soft object flat.

name: press-flatten
concept: The element is pressed down from the bottom until it is flat, widening slightly before it fades away. A heavier version of squashing flat.

name: collapse-left
concept: The element's width collapses toward its left edge, like a curtain drawn shut from the right side. Use it for closing a sidebar or panel.

name: collapse-right
concept: The element's width collapses toward its right edge, like a panel sliding shut from the left side. Use it for closing a right-hand drawer.

name: collapse-horizontal-fade
concept: The element shrinks to zero width from its center while it fades out. A softer, symmetric version of a horizontal collapse.

name: pinch-shut
concept: The element pinches inward from both sides while bulging slightly taller, then it vanishes. Like fabric pinched closed in the middle.

name: curtain-close
concept: The element narrows in slowing stages toward one edge, like a curtain drawn shut. Good for a wide banner or a modal backdrop panel.

name: deflate
concept: The element shrinks unevenly on each axis in turn, like a balloon losing air a little at a time. A soft, organic shrink rather than a uniform scale.

name: deflate-wobble
concept: The element shrinks while it wobbles side to side, as if it is losing air unevenly and tipping over. A livelier version of a deflate.

name: deflate-sideways
concept: The element leans to one side as it shrinks, like a punctured object sagging while it collapses. It combines a skew with an uneven scale.

name: punctured
concept: The element dips suddenly in size first, then it trails off into a slow final shrink. Like something punctured that loses air fast, then slowly.

name: air-let-out
concept: The element flattens vertically while it widens slightly, like a balloon slowly losing air and settling flat on a surface.

name: sag-deflate
concept: The element sags downward while it shrinks, like fabric losing its shape and drooping as it collapses.

name: wither
concept: The element fades out while it droops downward and tilts slightly, like a flower wilting on its stem.

name: droop-fade
concept: The element sinks downward and shortens as it fades, with no rotation. A heavier, straighter droop than a wither.

name: wilt
concept: The element tilts and shrinks around its base corner while it fades, like a stem bending as it wilts.

name: slump
concept: The element settles downward and widens slightly before it fades, like posture slumping under its own weight.

name: fade-and-droop
concept: The element fades out first, with only a small downward drift near the end. The fade leads, and the droop is a quiet finishing touch.

name: tired-fade
concept: The element rotates and sinks to one side while it fades, as if it is running out of energy.

name: crumble
concept: The element's opacity and size drop in distinct stages instead of smoothly, like it is crumbling apart piece by piece.

name: crumble-shrink
concept: The element shrinks and fades in three abrupt jumps rather than smoothly, like a structure giving way stage by stage.

name: disintegrate-steps
concept: The element fades and shrinks along a stepped timing curve, so the motion happens in visible discrete jumps, like frame-by-frame disintegration.

name: flicker-fade
concept: The element's opacity flickers unevenly before it settles to fully gone, like a dying light before it shrinks away.

name: stutter-fade
concept: The element's scale stutters slightly back and forth as its opacity drops, like a signal losing sync before it disappears.

name: fragment-fade
concept: The element rocks side to side in small rotations while it shrinks and fades, like it is breaking into fragments.

name: crumble-fall
concept: The element sinks downward in stages while it shrinks and fades, like debris crumbling and falling away.

name: dissolve
concept: The element softly blurs while it fades out, like it is dissolving into the background.

name: dissolve-soft
concept: The element dissolves slowly with a light blur and a barely noticeable shrink. A gentler, slower dissolve for calmer moments.

name: blur-fade
concept: The element blurs sharply first, then it fades, so its shape turns soft before it disappears.

name: mist-fade
concept: The element expands slightly while it blurs and fades, like it is turning into mist that spreads and thins.

name: haze-out
concept: The element brightens and blurs as it fades, like heat haze washing the shape out.

name: fog-dissolve
concept: The element spreads wider and drifts down slightly while it blurs away, like fog settling and dispersing.

name: soft-focus-out
concept: The element pulls back out of focus while it shrinks slightly, like a camera losing focus on the subject.

name: fold-away
concept: The element collapses vertically while it skews, like a hinged panel folding flat and away.

name: fold-up
concept: The element folds upward from its base with a skew, like a flap closing from below.

name: fold-down
concept: The element folds downward in two stages, skewing further as it closes, like a lid folding shut.

name: paper-fold
concept: The element narrows in two folds with alternating skew, like a sheet of paper being folded flat.

name: fold-flat
concept: The element flattens almost completely before it fades at the very last moment, like paper pressed flat.

name: crease-fold
concept: The element creases sharply at first, then it slowly finishes closing, like a fold pressed into shape.

name: evaporate
concept: The element grows slightly and rises while it fades, like it is evaporating into the air.

name: evaporate-rise
concept: The element rises steadily and expands while it thins out. A stronger, more visible version of evaporating.

name: steam-off
concept: The element rises, expands, and blurs as it fades, like steam drifting up and dispersing.

name: rise-and-fade
concept: The element drifts upward while it fades, with only a small increase in size. A simple, calm upward exit.

name: puff-away
concept: The element puffs outward quickly, then it rises and fades, like a small puff of smoke dispersing.

name: vanish-upward
concept: The element rises with a slight rotation while it thins out, like it is vanishing upward into nothing.
